messages.content: I would like to order a burger with the following modification verbatim: no onions, extra cheese

function.name: change_food
function.description: Modifies the food item based on the customer's request, such as changing ingredients or preparation methods. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

modification_request.description: Specific request detailing the changes to be made to the food item, such as 'no peanuts' or 'extra spicy'. If there are multiple requests, separate using comma with no space between comma

They said "verbatim: no onions, extra cheese". So we pass exactly that? But note instruction says if multiple requests, separate using comma with no space after comma. That means "no onions,extracheese"? Actually they'd say "no onions,extra cheese"? There's still a space before "cheese". We should remove spaces around commas but keep inside words maybe. Let's produce "no onions,extracheese"? No, that's wrong because it merges words incorrectly.

Better interpret: For each request separated by comma without space. Eg "no peanuts,extra spicy". In our case two modifications: "no onions" and "extra cheese". Should combine into one string: "no onions,extracheese"? This removes space between "onions," and "extracheese". But then "extracheese" loses space between "extra" and "cheese".

But spec might mean just no spaces after comma; internal spacing remains. Example given: 'no peanuts' or 'extra spicy', so combined could be 'no peanuts,extra spicy'? That's ambiguous. I'd follow example: use comma with no space after comma, but preserve inner word separation. So "no onions,extra cheese". Yes that matches pattern: first part has space within phrase, second also. There is no space after comma. Good.

Thus call function accordingly.
